newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - June 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - June 27.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The outgoing Legislative Council passed five bills significantly boosting workers' rights. Legislators representing the business sector said they will lobby future Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa to scrap the bills.

-- EXPRESS NEWS - Chinese President Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng will stay in Hong Kong's Hunghom district, across the harbour from the handover ceremony venue, and will travel to the ceremony by water to avoid confronting demonstrators directly.

-- APPLE DAILY -- A survey showed 40 percent of Hong Kong college students wished the territory was not going back to China on July 1 because they were worried that corruption would get worse and freedom would be restricted.

-- MING PAO -- Sources said the total amount in the Land Fund would reach HK$180 billion on handover day. Adding the Exchange Fund, the assets of the Hong Kong government will reach HK$715 billion, meaning HK$110,000 per Hong Kong person.

-- The Hong Kong Government is spending HK$500 million on handover celebrations, but surveys showed most Hong Kong people thought it was too much and said they would not participate. Some said the money should be spent on housing for "cagemen".
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL - The Bank of China said the Hong Kong handover would bring positive effects to the economy, and raised its economic growth estimate to 5.8 percent.

-- TA KUNG PO -- Chinese officials in charge of relations with Taiwan held a meeting on the Hong Kong handover, saying the return of Hong Kong would accelerate reunification with Taiwan. They expressed hope that Taiwan would enhance understanding of the "one country, two systems" formula.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The Hong Kong Monetary Authority was becoming increasingly concerned about Hong Kong's property market and was considering tightening the mortgage lending ceiling to curb speculation.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Chinese sources said Chinese warships and fighters will patrol waters and airspace off Hong Kong in coming days as Beijing stepped up security measures nationwide to prevent any hitches during the handover ceremony.
